lesson.title: Food Webs: A More Complete Picture
lesson.subject: science

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you built one food chain. Today: connect multiple food chains into a real food web!

Real ecosystems are more complex than one single food chain — a fox doesn't just eat rabbits, it might also eat mice or birds, and a rabbit might be eaten by a fox OR a hawk. A food web connects many overlapping food chains, showing these real multiple connections. Add a second animal to yesterday's food chain: what's another animal that might also eat grass, or that might also eat rabbits?
You just started building a real food web with multiple connections! Tomorrow we'll focus on decomposers' essential role.

objectives: Understand a food web as multiple overlapping food chains
Add a realistic second organism to extend yesterday's food chain into a small web
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's grass/rabbit/fox food chain.
2. Introduce food webs as multiple connected chains.
3. Have the child add a second animal (like a hawk or mouse) to build a small web.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's decomposers lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide a short list of real options (hawk, mouse, deer) to choose from rather than requiring the child to invent an animal
Ready for more: ask the child to draw their small food web with arrows showing all the energy connections
This is a genuine step up in complexity from yesterday's single chain — name that progression explicitly
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended extension activity — check that the child adds a real, ecologically sensible second animal (like a hawk that also eats rabbits, or a mouse that also eats grass).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS Grade 5 Life Science standard 5-LS2-1, extending yesterday's simple food-chain model into a more realistic food-web structure.
